Corollary 1. If f'(x) > 0 for all x in an interval I, then f is strictly increasing in I.
Corollary 2. If f'(x) < 0 for all x in an interval I, then f is strictly decreasing in I.
(f'(x) >= 0 or f'(x) <= 0, then “strictly” is removed)
Corollary 3. If f'(x) = 0 for all x in an interval I, then f is constant in I.

Name: Kritiska punkter/Critical points
Basic relationship:
If f is defined on an open interval (a, b) and assumes its maximum (or minimum) at a point c in (a, b) and f ′(c) exists, then f ′(c) = 0.
f' = 0 are called critical or stationary points (kritiska eller stationära punkter).

f'(x) > 0: Increasing
f'(x) < 0: Decreasing
f'(x) = 0: Extreme point(Maximum/Minimum) or terrace point:
1. Detect using second derivative
  1. f''(x) > 0: Minimum point
  2. f''(x) < 0: Maximum point
  3. f''(x) = 0: Terrace point
2. Detect using sign table
f''(x) = 0: Inflection point (either increasing or decreasing, check first derivative)
f''(x) > 0: Convex
f''(x) < 0: Concave

Name: L'hopital rule
Basic relationship:
lim{x->a, f(x)/g(x)} = lim{x->a, f'(a)/g'(a)}, in "0/0" or "\inf/\inf"
lim{x->a, f(x)/g(x)} = lim{x->a, (f(x)-0)/(g(x)-0)} = lim{x->a, (f(x)-f(a))/(g(x)-g(a))} = lim{x->a, ((f(x)-f(a))/(x-a))/((g(x)-g(a))/(x-a))} = lim{x->a, f'(a)/g'(a)}
